title: OpenStax Calculus Volume 1, 6.5 Physical Applications: Determine the mass of a one-dimensional object from its linear density function.
summary: OpenStax Calculus Volume 1, 6.5 Physical Applications: Determine the mass of a one-dimensional object from its linear density function.
body: OpenStax Calculus Volume 1, section "6.5 Physical Applications", prints these objectives: "Determine the mass of a one-dimensional object from its linear density function." "Determine the mass of a two-dimensional circular object from its radial density function." "Calculate the work done by a variable force acting along a line." "Calculate the work done in pumping a liquid from one height to another." "Find the hydrostatic force against a submerged vertical plate.". The section text says: "In this section, we examine some physical applications of integration. Let’s begin with a look at calculating mass from a density function. We then turn our attention to work, and close the section with a study of hydrostatic force." This card reports that page. The objectives are the book's learning statements, not a separate proof.
